subject: maths
title: Converting units of length, area and volume

scenes.heading: Converting units of length, area and volume
scenes.say: Everyone knows one metre is one hundred centimetres. So is one square metre one hundred square centimetres? Not even close! Let's find out why area and volume conversions are different.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A 1 m tile with a grid of 1 cm squares drawn on it
scenes.breaks: You can't always draw a neat grid, like on a circle, but the rule still works for every shape.
scenes.say: Picture a floor tile one metre by one metre. Draw a grid of one centimetre squares on it. There are one hundred squares along each edge, and one hundred rows. That's ten thousand little squares. So one square metre is ten thousand square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Picture a 1 m by 1 m tile with a grid of 1 cm squares. There are 100 along each edge and 100 rows: 10 000 squares. So 1 m² = 10 000 cm².

scenes.heading: 1 cm² = 100 mm²
scenes.say: Now a one centimetre square. Each side is ten millimetres, so it holds ten rows of ten. That's one hundred square millimetres.
scenes.caption: Each side is 10 mm, so 10 rows of 10: 1 cm² = 100 mm².

scenes.heading: Square it for area, cube it for volume
scenes.say: For length, use the factor once. For area, use it twice, so one square metre is ten thousand square centimetres. For volume, use it three times, so one cubic metre is a million cubic centimetres. A hectare is ten thousand square metres. And one cubic metre holds a thousand litres.
scenes.caption: Length: factor once. Area: twice, so 1 m² = 10 000 cm². Volume: three times, so 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³. 1 ha = 10 000 m². 1 m³ holds 1000 L.

scenes.heading: Area example
scenes.question: Convert 3.5 m² to cm².
lines: m² → cm²: big to small, so multiply
scenes.say: Convert three point five square metres to square centimetres. Big unit to small unit, so multiply. One square metre is ten thousand square centimetres. Three point five times ten thousand is thirty-five thousand square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Convert 3.5 m² to cm². Big to small, so multiply. 1 m² = 10 000 cm². 3.5 × 10 000 = 35 000 cm².

scenes.heading: Paddock in hectares
scenes.question: A paddock is 350 m long and 120 m wide. Find its area in hectares.
scenes.say: A paddock is three hundred and fifty metres by one hundred and twenty metres. That's forty-two thousand square metres. A hectare is ten thousand square metres, so divide by ten thousand. The paddock is four point two hectares.
scenes.caption: 350 m × 120 m = 42 000 m². 1 ha = 10 000 m², so 42 000 ÷ 10 000 = 4.2 ha.

scenes.heading: Convert every length first
scenes.say: Here's the tank. The length is in metres, but the width and height are in centimetres. Convert first, then multiply.
scenes.caption: The length is in metres, the width and height in centimetres. Convert first, then multiply.

scenes.heading: Fish tank in litres
scenes.question: A tank is 1.2 m long, 50 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres does it hold?
scenes.say: A fish tank is one point two metres long, fifty centimetres wide and forty centimetres high. Convert first: one point two metres is one hundred and twenty centimetres. The volume is two hundred and forty thousand cubic centimetres, which is the same number of millilitres. Divide by a thousand: two hundred and forty litres.
scenes.caption: 1.2 m = 120 cm. 120 × 50 × 40 = 240 000 cm³ = 240 000 mL. Divide by 1000: 240 L.

scenes.heading: Watch the little number

right.title: Volume (³)
points: Use the length factor three times

scenes.say: The little number on the unit tells you what to do. A two means area, so use the length factor twice. A three means volume, so use it three times. If units are mixed, convert the lengths first, then multiply.

points: Convert lengths first if units are mixed
scenes.say: Quick recap. For area, square the length factor. For volume, cube it. A hectare is ten thousand square metres, and one cubic metre is a thousand litres. When units are mixed, convert the lengths first. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: For area, square the length factor. For volume, cube it. 1 ha = 10 000 m², and 1 m³ = 1000 L. When units are mixed, convert lengths first. Now try the practice questions!
